html:
The longest river in British Columbia, Canada, about 1,375 kilometres long. It rises in the Rocky Mountains, runs through a deep canyon and reaches the sea just south of Vancouver.

It is one of the world's great salmon rivers, and its runs fed the peoples along it: the Lheidli T'enneh at what is now Prince George, the St'át'imc in the dry canyon, where salmon were wind-dried on racks, and the Stó:lō, Kwantlen and Musqueam of the Coast Salish world near the mouth.

Simon Fraser of the North West Company went down it to the sea in 1808. The Hudson's Bay Company built Fort Langley on the lower river in 1827. A gold rush in 1858 brought some thirty thousand miners, and Britain made the mainland the colony of British Columbia that year. The Canadian Pacific Railway was blasted through the canyon in the 1880s; in 1914 a rockslide from railway work at Hells Gate blocked the salmon runs for decades.
sum: The longest river in British Columbia, Canada, about 1,375 kilometres long. It rises in the Rocky Mountains, runs through a deep canyon and reaches the sea just south of Vancouver.
